newsitem.title: GERMANY: Early '98 budget to boost Italy credibility - Ciamp.
newsitem.headline: Early '98 budget to boost Italy credibility - Ciamp.

text.p: Italy's Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Saturday that a decision to bring forward the 1998 budget would send an important signal about Italy's intentions to get its finances in order.

"The advantage of anticipating the budget bill would be that of sending a message of continuity in Italy's policy to balance public accounts," Ciampi told reporters in Berlin where he was meeting partners from the G7 group of the world's most industrialised nations.
He added this would be "a message that would be greater than that which would be given if the budget were presented as usual in the fall."

Italy has made it clear that it plans to be among the first nations to join Europe's currency union in 1999 despite some concerns, also among its partners, over its relatively poor record in sustaining fiscal prudence.
The idea of bringing forward the budget has been discussed with Prime Minister Romano Prodi, Ciampi said, adding: "Now we will see if it comes through. Parliamentary agreement on this is necessary,"
